searchText: Hello, my name is Giovanny and I applied to the Core Development program. Glad to see initiatives like this one, find communities willing to help people learn and get involved into the protocol development. I'll be exploring the discord and channels in the meantime, have learned already a ton of things just by poking around inside conversation threads. Cheers! I'm really intereseted in applying to this but I don't know too much about core dev...what are some resources I can learn to learn more about the core protocol? I've recently started learning about dapps and smart contracts, but I understand that's not core stuff. I started out learning about bitcoin blockchain, and how blockchain tech works, but where can I learn more about eth protocol? (i've read white paper and started yellow) what does the eth protocol consist of? <@755612893046636585> check the pins in the channel. thanks doc hi all - some great links being shared here, so creating this Notion doc to keep track of relevant and interesting materials, hope its helpful https://www.notion.so/Core-Developer-Apprenticeship-Program-Cohort-Links-bf9493bc826f42f7b3e530c33c8539d6 great resource, thanks for putting this together! I am planning to apply but I have yet to figure out which topics in mind or decided on the projects proposed in the github repo. will it be Ok if I apply first and let you know in this channel? or will it be a big part of the application You don't need to know what you want to work on prior to applying, so go ahead and get your application in Seconding the appreciation for putting this together and sharing it. If you're feeling bold, feel free to PR anything into the `cohort-zero` repository that isn't already there. Hello, my name is Ognyan, I have ~3 years experience with software engineering. I have been working mainly with Python, Ruby and Clojure, experimenting with Rust too. Crypto holder since 2017. Recently I started to learn more about the blockchain ecosystem and tooling, I would love to dive deep into Ethereum protocol and have some fun. Hello everyone, I am odysseas, currently leading DevRel at Netdata. I had an intermittent relationship with the blockchain space since 2018, but after reading "The Sovereign Individual", I am certain that this is the space I want to contribute into. Right now, I am mostly interested in L2 scaling, MEV and generally how changes in the protocol can affect the mechanism design / crypto economics. I started learning Soildity recently and I am compiling a handful of resources. Although not directly relevant to protocol design/implementation, you might be interested 🤷‍♂️ https://dev.to/odyslam/learning-solidity-in-public-58a3 Hey <@!364458974906548225> I have a couple of resources that are *somewhat* related to protocol, such as blog posts about scaling, MEV, etc. Would they be appropriate for a PR? Like populate suggested reading for individual areas that could possibly interest others. I just added some subsections in the recommended read me you can check out. I think scaling fits in. But you can always add them in your own notes file if it isn't directly related. TBH I did not know what those notes are. Can anyone creates them? Yeah, I think scaling and MEV, since the more I read the more I understand how important it can be. The tricky part is what the resources should be since for exampel, I have read a couple of very well written pieces by Paradigm's blog, which I guess wouldn't be appropriate Fork the repo, then you can add a notes file then put in a pull request when you want to add it. Anyone can add them 😄 So anyone can create a small personal space to share notes. Interesting Thanks <@!843901716926955623> for the context 🙂 <@!843901716926955623> done. Let me know if the links i have added are appropriate done!
